Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of the discussion:
- You described product recommendation traffic (user prompts -> 1-2 model calls) with spiky peaks around new feature rollouts.
- Main concerns: predictable latency during peaks, noisy-neighbor performance impacts on shared infrastructure, and data residency for US-East.

Redwood options (high level):
1) Hosted API: fast to get started, pay-as-you-go. We have several isolation mitigations (workload-aware routing, KV prefix caching, per-tenant fair-share), but there is some multi-tenant sharing that can lead to increased tail latency under extreme global spikes.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for your account. Provides hard isolation for model serving (dedicated instances, isolated queues) and predictable throughput/SLOs. Recommended when latency SLOs and predictable unit economics matter.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation and control (required for regulated data / strict compliance).

Noisy-neighbor specifics you asked about:
- For Dedicated we pin model instances to reserved GPUs and isolate request queues per-customer; you get predictable p95/p99 behavior and can set capacity to meet p99 SLOs.
- For Hosted we use smart routing + admission controls and autoscaling, plus per-customer cache warmers to mitigate cold-starts. We also offer fallback routes to model variants when capacity is constrained.

What we need from you to size a short pilot and produce a ballpark cost/SLA proposal:
- Typical and peak QPS (requests/sec)
- Average tokens in / tokens out per request (or sample CSV)
- Target latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and any hard SLA requirement
- Data residency / encryption / compliance constraints

Next steps: if you can share the quick traffic sample (CSV) and SLO numbers, Marissa will produce a dedicated-sizing estimate and we can schedule a 30-45 minute follow-up to walk the numbers and propose a pilot. Attached: prod-traffic-sample.csv (sample format) and redwood-isolation-whitepaper.pdf (brief on how we isolate noisy neighbors).

Proposed windows for follow-up: Mon 23 Feb 9-11am PT or Tue 24 Feb 1-3pm PT. Which works for you?

Thanks — Priyom

Hi Alice — Marissa here (solutions). Wanted to address the noisy-neighbor / p99 question directly and give an initial sizing recommendation for a pilot.

Isolation & tail behavior (short answer):
- Dedicated capacity: hard isolation. Your models run on reserved GPU instances and we isolate request queues per-customer. In our experience with customers with similar QPS and prompt sizes, p99 is stable and primarily driven by internal model latency (token generation) rather than cross-tenant interference — as long as the reserved capacity matches peak concurrency. You can expect p99 latency within ~1.1x of model-native generation time under typical production spikes.
- Hosted API: we mitigate noisy neighbors with prioritized routing, per-tenant rate shaping, admission controls, and proactive cache warmers. This works well for many customers, but under correlated global spikes you may see occasional tail increases since resources are shared. We provide historical tail percentiles per-tenant so you can evaluate risk prior to committing.

Sizing + pilot recommendation (based on your numbers):
- Peak 20 req/s, avg tokens ~150 total. For a recommendation surface and to meet p99 < 800ms we suggest starting with a dedicated pool equivalent to 2x A100-80GB-class GPUs (baseline), with autoscale policy to add up to 4 GPUs during sustained bursts. That gives headroom for concurrent generation and KV cache warmups.
- Pilot scope: 2-week pilot in US-East, dedicated pool, synthetic replay of your traffic + small production shadowing. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99, token-level costs, and error rates.
- Ballpark cost for pilot (monthly pro-rata): we'll follow up with a formal estimate but expect a mid-four-figure monthly pro-rata; we'll include a numeric ballpark on the follow-up call once we size exact model/quantization choices. Attached is a preliminary dedicated-sizing-estimate.xlsx.

Next steps:
1) Priyom — locking Tue 24 Feb 1pm PT for the kickoff.
2) Alice — please share the CSV sample when convenient.
3) We'll prepare a short pilot statement of work and a sizing/cost slide for the call.

Happy to answer any technical follow-ups ahead of the call.

Best,
